description: attn's commands to track, report or hand off work, and to reach the user and other agents.

do.title: Run attn commands
do.description:
Runs a script of attn's commands and answers with what it returns or logs, then with what it changed. Each command is a function that takes one object of named arguments and returns its result:

const plan = seed_plant({title: "Retry uploads", body: `Retry the upload twice.`});
for (const id of ["s-7k3f9m", "s-2w4x8p"]) {
  try {
    seed_harvest({seed: id, reason: "Shipped"});
  } catch (e) {
    console.log(id, e.code, e.message);
  }
}
return plan.id;

- A result is the object that `attn <command> --json` prints, or a string when the command answers with text. `return` or console.log what you want to read. A script that does neither answers with each read's result.
- The script is plain JavaScript, with no files, network, timers or modules.
- Put long text in a template literal, and in it write each \ as \\, each ` as \` and each ${ as \${. attn stores the text the literal makes, so an unescaped \t is stored as a tab and ${NAME} fails.
- A refused command throws a Refusal with `code`, `message`, `fix` and `command`. When nothing catches it, the script ends there. A script is not a transaction: the commands before the refusal stand, so run only the rest again.
- The answer ends with `changed:` and a line for each command that changed something: the arguments it sent, then `->` and what it answered, such as a new seed's id. Check that the arguments are what you meant, above all values the script cut out of other text. A script that only changes things needs no `return` or console.log.
- One call runs at most 1,000 commands and 50 s.

The commands agents call most, with ? on an optional argument, are below. Call these without reading about them first: a refusal about arguments names them all. Every other attn command is a function too; read its rules with `skill({command: "seed_park"})`, or a family's signatures with `skill({command: "crew"})`, before you first call it.

instructions:
attn runs the commands below. Call them as functions in a script: `attn_do` runs any of them, `attn_read` those that only read. `ask` and `skill` are also tools of their own. Find a command by the words below. Call a command that `attn_do` shows a signature for. Before you first call any other, read its row's reference, named in parentheses, with `skill({reference: "…"})`, or its rules with `skill({command: "…"})`. For `guide X`, call `guide({topic: "X"})`.

- See what each agent is doing now: activity
- See or message other agents by name; read your inbox: agent_list, agent_peek, agent_msg, agent_inbox (converse-and-observe)
- Close or reload an agent, wrap up, or close yourself: agent_close, agent_reload (wrap-up)
- Ask the user a decision only they can make: ask, ask_list, ask_amend, ask_close
- Run an agent on a schedule or event: automation_list, automation_apply (guide automations)
- Use the in-app browser: browser_open, browser_snapshot (browser)
- Point at something in the app: callout_anchors, callout_show (callouts)
- Work with permanent agents (crew) and their charters: crew_list, crew_start (charter, guide crew)
- Start another agent on work you may hand off, and look up one you started: delegate, delegate_status (delegation)
- Read or change delegation roles' models and harnesses: delegate_roles, delegate_roles_set, delegate_roles_rollback (delegation-roles)
- Answer the user's questions about attn: guide
- File a crew member's letter: handoff
- Read the Notebook with your file tools, or add to its journal: journal_append (notebook)
- List every session and profile: list
- Set up code navigation for a language: nav_status, nav_set (code-navigation)
- Show or finish the Chief's onboarding: onboarding (onboarding)
- Show the user a markdown document or a seed: open (markdown)
- Deliver through pull requests or trunk; record or watch a pull request: pr_record, pr_watch (delivery)
- Your session and the seeds it works on: presence
- Present a change for review, or answer about it: review_start, review_check, review_answer (review)
- Find work to pick up; read or claim a seed or plan: seed_ready, seed_show, seed_tend (garden)
- Record progress, report delegated work, prove a check: seed_note, seed_check_report (delegated-agent)
- Finish, pause, abandon or give back a seed: seed_harvest, seed_park, seed_wither, seed_replant
- Track new work, find existing work, split a plan: seed_search, seed_plant, seed_plot, seed_link (garden)
- Change a seed's body, checks, files or reminders: seed_edit, seed_check_add, seed_attach, seed_remind
- Wait for a time, a pull request or a seed, with your session closed: seed_standby (garden)
- Update a seed's pulse or bed: seed_pulse, seed_bed_ls, seed_bed_assign
- Read past sessions; rename, snooze or unsnooze one: session_list, session_transcript, session_rename, session_snooze, session_unsnooze (converse-and-observe)
- Read or change attn's settings: settings_list, settings_get, settings_set
- Read a capability's rules: skill
- Write more than a few sentences for a reader: skill (showing)
- Find out why a session shows its state: state_explain
- Open a shell, run in it, read a terminal, move between desktops: terminal_open, terminal_run, terminal_read, terminal_move (terminal)
- Bring the user to you after a notification: turn_open
- Report what got in your way: vent

An update about a seed asks you to read what changed. Act only when it needs you or the user.
name: attn

read.title: Read with attn commands
read.description: Runs a script as attn_do does, with the same functions, but refuses a command that changes something. It needs no permission, so read with it: `return seed_show({seed: "s-7k3f9m"})`. Read several things in one script, and return only the parts you need once you know a result's fields.

tools.name: activity
tools.title: what each agent is doing, and why nothing is generated
tools.description: Shows whether activity lines are generated and why not when they are not: the presence tier (nothing is generated while nobody can see it), the setting, and whether an agent is chosen to write them. Then each session that generates a line, with its line, its age and why its last run failed.

tools.name: activity_clear
tools.title: forget one session's line and its read position
tools.description: Forgets one session's activity line and its read position, so the next line is written from what happens next.

id.description: the name, short id, full id or unique prefix of the live session

tools.name: agent_list
tools.title: the address book of every session on this daemon
tools.description: The address book: every session on this daemon with its short id, name, profile, state, and whether a turn is owed. Inside attn it lists your session's profile. Read-only.

tools.name: agent_peek
tools.title: observe a session without interrupting it
tools.description: Observes a session without interrupting it: state, last assistant message, and the rendered screen. On a Claude session, says when the composer holds Claude's suggestion and not typed text. Passive: the observed agent never notices. `target` is a crew name, a live session's name, a short id, a full session id, or a unique session id prefix. A crew member between sessions stays between sessions.

target.description: a crew name, a live session's name, a short id, a full session id, or a unique id prefix

tools.name: agent_msg
tools.title: send a session, crew member or seed a message
tools.description: Sends a session, crew member or seed a message. By default the message waits until the recipient's turn ends: the body stays in the inbox and the recipient gets a generic inbox notification at its next safe prompt. `steer` puts the message into a working recipient's running turn at its next step, without stopping the turn. `interrupt` stops a working recipient's turn now and makes the message its next prompt. A recipient that is not working gets the message right away either way. A harness that cannot take a steer or an interrupt keeps the message queued, and the result says why. `as_user` delivers the text as the user's own words, without the sender's name; use it only to pass on words the user gave you to pass on. The result says queued, notified, steered, interrupted, or refused. attn starts a session for a member between sessions before the notification is placed. A seed id reaches its current or next tender, waiting when none is reachable.
tools.signature: agent_msg({target, text, steer?: true, interrupt?: true, as_user?: true})

as_user.description: deliver the text as the user's words, without your name; only to pass on what the user said

interrupt.description: stop the recipient's turn now and make the message its next prompt

steer.description: put the message into the recipient's running turn at its next step, without stopping the turn

target.description: a live session's name, a session's short id, full id or unique prefix, a crew member's name, or a seed id

tools.name: agent_close
tools.title: close a session for good, with a reason
tools.description:
Closes a session for good. A session may close itself and agents below it in its delegation chain, including delegates of delegates. The profile's Chief may close any agent of that profile. The reason is required because the session row stays in the ledger, and the reason is what the next reader gets. Without `compact` the close is immediate, so say what you have to say first. Pass a session's name or id, a seed id to close whoever tends it, or `self` to close yourself with no target.

When a session closes, each seed it tends keeps its tender and gets a note about the close. When `garden_v2_enabled` is on, closing another session instead parks its growing seeds that are not on standby. Seeds on standby still keep their tender with a note.

Closing yourself refuses in two cases, while a close by another session goes through. First, closing yourself refuses while you have an open ask that nobody can answer after the close, and names each one. That covers an ask about no seed, which the close withdraws, or one on a seed with no other tender or standby. End your turn and wait for the answer, or withdraw the ask with `ask_close`. Second, when `garden_v2_enabled` is on, closing yourself refuses while you tend a growing seed that is not on standby. Harvest, park, wither, or put each one on standby first. With `compact`, both checks run again once the compact has an outcome. An ask opened or a growing seed kept before then keeps the session open, and attn leaves a notice in your inbox naming why.

`compact` goes only with `self`: attn waits for your turn to end, compacts your conversation through the harness, then closes the session. End your turn right after: you get no turn after the compact. When the compact fails, the session still closes, and the reason says the compact did not run. Only a Claude session with the Claude mod and a Codex session on the shared Codex app server compact, on the home machine or an outpost, and a Sigma session on the home machine; attn refuses any other session and says why. Compact only a session that will resume as itself, as a seed's tender does when its standby resumes it. A crew member's next session starts fresh.
tools.signature: agent_close({target?, reason, self?: true, compact?: true})

compact.description: compact the conversation after this turn, then close (with self)

target.description: a live session's name, its short id, full id or unique prefix, or the seed whose tender to close

tools.name: agent_reload
tools.title: interrupt and reload agents in place
tools.description: Interrupts and reloads agents in place, as "Reload this agent" does. Running work is interrupted and non-persistent state may be lost. Short ids, full ids, unique prefixes, and names of live sessions and of crew members in session work; a member between sessions stays between sessions. A member whose saved harness matches its session reloads with its saved model and effort. A session may reload itself and descendants; the profile's chief may reload any agent in that profile. `all` is chief-only, includes the chief and crew, and excludes shells. Chief and crew close protections do not prevent reload. Each target reports an outcome; failures leave successful reloads in place. Repeated targets reload once. Exited agents use 80x24. The caller reloads last if selected; a self reload may interrupt the command before its result arrives.

all.description: every agent in the caller's profile (chief only)

targets.description: the sessions or crew members to reload

tools.name: agent_inbox
tools.title: read your unread notifications, or one message by id
tools.description: Reads up to 20 unread notifications in FIFO order, or one notified user or peer message by `message`. Each returned item gets its durable read receipt. `limit` can be 1 through 50.

limit.description: how many unread items to read (default 20)

tools.name: agent_msg_status
tools.title: whether a message you sent is queued, notified or read
tools.description: Inspects a message you sent as queued, notified, or read, and says whether a running turn took it as a steer or an interrupt, still holds it, or it arrived as the next prompt instead, and whether you sent it as the user. A message the recipient's harness holds for its running turn reads as notified until the harness places it.

tools.name: agent_attachment
tools.title: download a file the user attached to a message
tools.description: Downloads a saved user file from this session's profile to `out`, then you can inspect it. Older messages quote a quick capture id before the attachment id; that form still works, and the second id is the attachment. Outside a session, choose the profile when more than one profile exists.

out.description: where to write the file; it must not exist yet; a relative path resolves against the folder the session started in

tools.name: ask
tools.title: open an ask in the user's queue; it returns at once
tools.description: Opens an ask in the user's queue and returns its id at once. Use it for a decision only the user can make, instead of stopping to ask in the conversation. The user reads it without this conversation. To ask permission for a risky action, name the exact action and its target in the question, such as the command, branch or environment. The answer approves only what the question names. Follow the "Asking the user" rules in your launch instructions. If you did not receive them, call `skill({reference: "ask"})` for how to write an ask, which visuals to show, and what to do afterward. The ask is markdown. Question blocks in it ask the user something; an ask without one just tells them something: `:::question` (pick one choice), `:::question-multi` (pick any number of choices), `:::question-text` (write an answer) and `:::question-file` (attach a screenshot or a file), each closed by `:::`. A block's first line is the question; the rest is context. Choices are "- [ ] label" or "- [ ] label — why"; "Recommended:

re.description: the earlier ask this one follows up; the user sees its question and their answer above this one

seed.description: a seed you tend that the ask is about (defaults to the seed your delegation assigned you)

subject.description: the ask's subject (defaults to its first question)

tools.name: ask_list
tools.title: your open asks and those about seeds you tend, then the open asks of the agents you oversee
tools.description: Lists your open asks and those about seeds you tend, then, apart from yours, the open asks of the agents you oversee.

tools.name: ask_show
tools.title: one ask, with who asked, its seed, its age and text
tools.description: Prints one open ask you hold or oversee: who asked, its seed, its age and its text.

tools.name: ask_amend
tools.title: add to an open ask when the facts change; the user keeps its place and their answer so far
tools.description:
Adds markdown to the end of an open ask you hold or oversee, when something it says has changed. The user sees the addition as an update with its time, and keeps the ask's place in their queue and the answer they have started. Closing the ask and asking again would throw both away.

An amendment renders markdown as the ask does, diagrams, tables and local images included, and carries no question blocks, so the ask's questions stay as they are; to ask something new, open another ask. Images resolve as they do when you open an ask, against the folder the ask was opened from; from another folder, name each image by its absolute path. An ask's images never change once saved: save a new picture under a new name, because attn refuses an amendment that names a saved image's path with different bytes. attn refuses an amendment to an ask the user already answered.

tools.name: ask_close
tools.title: withdraw an ask you no longer need answered
tools.description: Withdraws an ask you no longer need answered. To withdraw an ask of an agent you oversee, say why in `reason`: attn notes the reason on the ask's seed and tells the agent that asked, so it does not wait for an answer.

reason.description: why you withdraw an ask of an agent you oversee; required for those, and sent to the asker

tools.name: automation_run
tools.title: start a run now
tools.description: Starts a run of the automation now and prints it. The CLI prints the run once its session is launched. A tool call answers once the run is recorded, pending, while preparing its location, which for a repository_worktree automation can mean a first clone, and launching its session go on; `automation runs` shows how it went. A run whose preparation fails in a way that can be retried, such as a failed clone or a GitHub host that is not signed in, stays pending: the same `request_id` delivers it again, and the CLI prints the reason. Until the run is delivered, `automation runs` shows the latest such reason as its `last_error` and how many attempts failed as its `failed_attempts`. `input` is the occurrence's structured input; `pr_url` resolves one GitHub pull request into it instead, for a repository_worktree automation. A retry with the same `request_id` returns the run the first request started.

The session's opening includes its charter location, latest handoff, home instructions, held seeds with handoff notes, and ready counts for their plots. `agent` overrides the harness for this session. tools.name: delegate
tools.title: start another agent on work you may hand off
tools.description:
Starts another agent in its own session, which the user can open and steer. Every delegation has a seed, which the delegated agent reads when it starts: `brief` plants a new one, and `seed` uses an existing seed's current assignment. `handover` transfers that seed to the new agent, with `note` as the next step; the previous agent keeps running. `authorization` says how far the user lets the task go, written as instructions to the agent; it is saved on the seed, and the opening delivers it. Without it, a delegation keeps the seed's current words.

`model` is required unless `role` or `fallback` picks the model from the user's delegation roles (`delegate_roles` lists them). `cwd` is the folder or repository on the target machine, `host` or the caller's own. Inside Git, choose one complete checkout: `reuse_checkout` with `branch`, `new_worktree` with `branch` and `from`, or `new_worktree` with `existing_branch`. Outside Git, `cwd` is enough. On the caller's own machine, a relative `cwd` resolves against the CLI's working directory, or the folder a tool caller's session started in. Only a handover's predecessor is exempt from checkout occupancy; any other active session there needs `allow_worktree_reuse`.

The command waits for the agent's first turn. Called as a tool, it waits at most 20 s and answers with the operation: `completed` with the session it started, or `failed` with the reason. `accepted` or `preparing` means that the agent has not taken its first turn. It is still starting, or stopped at a question that only someone else can answer, such as its folder-trust question; `progress` or your inbox names the question when attn can see it. Tell the user about a question it names, and otherwise go on with your work or end your turn. Do not call `delegate_status` to wait for it. A start that fails or stalls, and what the agent reports later, reaches your inbox. Pass the same `request_id` to retry safely: a retry returns the accepted operation instead of starting another.
tools.signature: delegate({brief?, seed?, priority?: true, handover?: true, note?, authorization?, host?, cwd?, reuse_checkout?: true, new_worktree?: true, branch?, from?, existing_branch?, worktree_path?, allow_worktree_reuse?: true, request_id?, agent?, model?, role?, choice?, fallback?: true, effort?, name?, desktop?, yolo?: true})

branch.description: the branch to reuse, or the new branch to create

brief.description: the task: plants a seed for new work

cwd.description: the folder or repository on that machine (required)

desktop.description: a desktop of your profile for the new agent: its shortcut digit (1-9), its name or its id; the agent opens at the end of that desktop's row without changing what you see (default: the caller's desktop)

effort.description: pin the effort; "default" selects the harness default (default: medium where supported)

existing_branch.description: a local branch for the new worktree

fallback.description: the configured model for work no role fits

from.description: the ref a new branch starts from

handover.description: transfer the seed to the new agent

host.description: the outpost to run on, by name or id; home selects the home (default: the caller's machine)

model.description: pin the model; "default" selects the harness default

name.description: the session's name, at most 48 characters (default: from the brief or the seed's title)

note.description: the handover note: the next step

priority.description: put the delegate's owed turns first

request_id.description: a stable retry key; op- is reserved (default: a new one, which the CLI prints)

reuse_checkout.description: use the checkout at cwd on branch

role.description: a configured delegation role, with its default choice

seed.description: an existing seed whose assignment the agent takes

tools.name: handoff

Files the letter closing this crew member's session. You write it; attn files it into handoffs/ in the member's home, with a UTC-stamped name, and never edits the prose. A correction is a new letter.

Filing ends the session, and the member is between sessions until its next session starts, whether or not the user is at the machine. When `crew_apply` asked this session for its letter because the member's harness changed, filing instead starts the next session on the new harness from the letter. The letter also records this session so attn can keep its transcript.

If the session cannot end or the next one cannot start, the letter stays filed and this session keeps running. `retry` tries again with that letter.

Only the member's own session can file one. The note for whoever tends a piece of work next is the other axis: a seed note marked as a handoff, with `seed_note`.

The result names the file and its hash after the append.

tools.name: pr_watch
tools.title: durably watch readiness and feedback
tools.description:
Records the pull request if needed and watches it until it merges or closes, or until `pr_unwatch`. Updates arrive in the agent inbox: state changes (ready, changes requested, failed checks, merged, closed), feedback (comments, review comments, review bodies, reopened review threads) and monitoring outages that last 10 minutes. The call returns at once.

`mode` says when the pull request is ready: green waits for passing checks, codex also for Codex's review, and formal-review for an approving review, from `reviewer` when given. Watching again changes the mode.

Because agents post as the user, a watch skips the feedback the user's GitHub account wrote. Feedback by others, including the author of a pull request under review, and state changes still reach the agent. A watch delivers the user's feedback too once the user sets `pull_requests.own_comments` to `ring`.

`seed` addresses the watch to the seed's tender; an unknown or closed seed is refused.

mode.description: when the pull request counts as ready: green (the default), codex or formal-review

reviewer.description: the reviewer whose approval counts, only with formal-review

seed.description: send the updates to whoever tends this seed

url.description: A pull request's URL, such as https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/12.

tools.description: Stops this session's watch of the pull request and clears its unread updates. The pull request stays recorded. With `seed`, stops the seed's watch instead.

seed.description: stop the watch addressed to this seed

url.description: A pull request's URL, such as https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/12.

tools.name: seed_search

Seeds carrying some words also appear. Ranks by title coverage, word coverage, relevance and recency, with a boost for open seeds. Prints status, last active and an original matching line. Search before you plant, so a duplicate is found instead of created.

tools.name: seed_plant

tools.description: Plants a seed and prints its id, slug and title. `body` takes markdown; if the seed gains children, that body is the plot's plan. `part_of` plants it under a plot. `bed` assigns a root seed to an existing curated bed when `garden_v2_enabled` is on (otherwise a root seed auto-routes by repository if a bed matches). `checks` defines what the seed must prove; attn numbers each check unless C#= names the id, and prints each id. Lists up to 3 similar open seeds in your profile, leaving out that plot. Planting always proceeds. If one is the same work, wither the new seed.

tools.name: seed_plot
tools.title: plant a whole plot in one move from a JSON payload
tools.description:
Plants a whole plot in one move from a JSON payload, read from the `plot` file, or from stdin when the file is - or omitted: {"title": …, "body": …, "bed": "<bed>", "checks": [{"id": "C5", "text": …, "shared": true}], "part_of": "<plot>", "discovered_from": "<seed>", "children": [{"title": …, "body": …, "checks": […], "after": ["<sibling step slug>"]}]}.

Children are parallel by default; `after` names the siblings a child waits for, by step slug or full title. `part_of` plants the plot inside another plot, and `discovered_from` records the seed whose work turned up the plot; give each by id or slug. `bed` assigns a root plot to an existing curated bed when `garden_v2_enabled` is on; children inherit their root plot's bed. A shared check is proven by each seed below the plot that has no children. The plot, its children and their edges commit together. Prints the plot's id and each child's id and step slug, then up to 3 similar open seeds across all planted titles, each naming the new seed it resembles. Planting always proceeds; wither a new seed if a suggestion is the same work.

id.description: You write it, such as C1, so the bodies can cite it.

plot.description: the plot payload to read; - or omitted reads stdin

bed.description: An existing curated bed to assign the crown to, by id, name or slug (requires garden_v2_enabled).

after.description: The siblings this child waits for, by step slug or full title.

discovered_from.description: The seed whose work turned up this plot, by id or slug.

part_of.description: A plot to plant this plot under, by id or slug.

a.description: A seed's id, such as s-7k3f9m, or its slug. A slug two seeds share is refused, listing each match.

b.description: A seed's id, such as s-7k3f9m, or its slug. A slug two seeds share is refused, listing each match.

tools.name: seed_unlink
tools.title: remove an edge between two seeds
tools.description: Removes the edge "a relation b". Every link has an unlink.

a.description: A seed's id, such as s-7k3f9m, or its slug. A slug two seeds share is refused, listing each match.

b.description: A seed's id, such as s-7k3f9m, or its slug. A slug two seeds share is refused, listing each match.

tools.name: seed_ready

With neither `plot` nor `all` the scope is your profile's garden, unless this session was dispatched at a plot, and then that plot; `all` steps back out to the garden.

plot.description: list every child of this plot

tools.name: seed_standby
tools.title: wait for seed mail with this session closed
tools.description:
Puts a seed you tend on standby with `next`, a note saying what to do next, and closes this session. When mail reaches the seed, attn resumes the session and delivers the note; for a crew member it starts a session. `in` and `at` also set the seed's reminder to that time, with the note as its message, as `seed_remind` does. When the session can compact, attn compacts it before closing; end your turn right after the command. `stay` keeps this session open.

attn refuses while the seed has mail you have not read; read it with `agent_inbox` first. attn also refuses to close the session while it has an open ask, about this seed, another seed or none, and names each ask: a wait on the user keeps the session open, so ask with `ask` and end your turn. When the user tells you to close while an ask about the seed is open, put the seed on standby with `stay`, then run `agent_close({self: true, …})`: the seed stays on standby, and the answer resumes you. When `garden_v2_enabled` is on, attn also refuses without `stay` while this session still tends another growing seed that is not on standby, leaving this seed unchanged: finish or park the others first, or pass `stay` on earlier seeds before putting the last one on standby to close.

Only the seed's tender sets standby, from its own session, and the seed stays claimed while the session is closed. A new standby replaces the note. Standby ends once you have read all of the seed's mail, and when the seed is parked, harvested, withered or gets a new tender. If the session closes before reading the mail, the mail resumes it again. `clear` ends standby and leaves the reminder.

Rows carry short ids, agent, state, owed or snoozed turns and seed slugs. A delegate whose dispatcher is closed or absent becomes a root. A closed agent whose seed is on standby stays under its dispatcher with the state standby, and its seed column adds what it waits for. Shell split provenance is labeled separately. Inside attn the tree is limited to your session's profile; `profile` narrows it. Only `profile` goes with `tree`.

Each id reports success or why it failed. session_unsnooze ends a snooze early.

ids.description: the names, short ids, full ids or unique prefixes of the sessions to snooze

tools.name: session_unsnooze
tools.title: end sessions' snoozes early
tools.description: Ends snoozes early, with the same permissions as session_snooze. Already unsnoozed is a successful no-op. session_list and session_show include the snoozed-until instant.

ids.description: the names, short ids, full ids or unique prefixes of the sessions to unsnooze

tools.name: session_rename
tools.title: give a session the name a person reads in the sidebar
tools.description: Gives a session the name a person reads in the sidebar and the ledger: a few plain words about the work, up to 48 characters. `target` defaults to the session running this command. Rename when the main work drifts from the name it started with.

name.description: the new name; quote it when it has spaces

target.description: the name, short id, full id or unique prefix of the live session to rename (defaults to the current session)

tools.name: session_reopen
tools.title: bring a closed or stopped session back under its own id
tools.description: Brings a closed or stopped session back under its own id, on its last or current desktop in its profile. Without `action` it performs the plain reopen and refuses, naming what is offered, when the verdict does not allow one. Actions that recreate a worktree or fetch a branch write to the repository and only ever run when named here. Sessions whose profile was deleted cannot reopen. To close a session, use agent_close.

action.description: reopen, recreate_worktree_and_reopen or fetch_recreate_and_reopen; session_show lists the ones offered

id.description: the short id, full id or unique prefix of the session to reopen

tools.name: settings_list
tools.title: show every setting's key, scope, value and description
tools.description: Shows each setting's key, scope, value and description. `all` adds the read-only values attn computes. `features` shows each experimental feature instead, whether it is on, and when a change applies.

all.description: include the read-only values attn computes

tools.name: settings_get
tools.title: show the value of one setting
tools.description: Shows the value in effect. It is empty when the setting is unset, unless the setting is on by default.

key.description: A setting's key, as settings list prints it.

tools.name: settings_set
tools.title: change a setting
tools.description: Changes a setting. An empty `value` restores the default of a setting that has one, or clears it where its description allows. On an outpost, a home setting is saved at the home.

key.description: A setting's key, as settings list prints it.

value.description: the new value; empty restores the default

tools.name: skill
tools.title: print the map of what attn can do, or a capability's rules
tools.description: Prints the map of what attn can do. `reference` prints one capability's rules instead, such as garden or delegation; read a capability's rules before you first use it. `list` prints the names of the bundled references, one per line. `command` prints one command's signature and rules, or the signatures of a family's commands. The text matches the running release.

command.description: print one command's rules, e.g. seed_harvest, or a family's signatures, e.g. crew

reference.description: print this capability's rules, e.g. garden

tools.name: state_explain
tools.title: replay the recorded state observations of one session
tools.description: Replays the daemon's recorded state observations for one session: which source claimed what, and whether the claim was applied, vetoed before the store, discarded by it, or skipped by its own source. Identical observations in a row fold into one with a count. Reading it changes nothing.

id.description: the name, short id, full id or unique prefix of the live session to explain

tools.name: terminal_ls
tools.title: list the terminals on your desktop, or on every desktop
tools.description: Lists the terminals of your desktop, or of the desktop `desktop` names, or with `all` of every desktop in your profile: each one's id, name, agent, state, desktop, position and the session that opened it.

all.description: list every desktop in your profile

desktop.description: list this desktop: its shortcut digit, its name or its id

tools.name: terminal_open
tools.title: open a shell beside you, or on a desktop or outpost
tools.description: Opens a shell at the end of your desktop's row, keeping the user's focus where it was, and returns its terminal id. `down` stacks it below you, or below the terminal you most recently opened in your column. `desktop` opens it on that desktop, creating a missing numbered one. `host` selects an outpost by name or id, or home; `cwd` names a directory on that machine, and without it a shell on another machine starts in its home directory. With `command`, open types the command once the shell shows its first OSC 133 prompt. Called as a tool, open answers at once and types the command when that prompt comes; if no prompt comes within 30 s, or the terminal ends or the daemon restarts first, nothing is typed and a notice in your inbox says so. If the daemon restarts while open types the command, the notice says the command may have run. On the CLI the command waits up to 30 s for that prompt and fails if none comes.
tools.signature: terminal_open({host?, down?: true, desktop?, cwd?, command?: ["…"]})

command.description: the command to type once the shell shows its first prompt; one word is typed as written, several are each quoted

cwd.description: the directory on the target machine

desktop.description: the desktop to open it on

host.description: the machine to open it on

tools.name: terminal_run
tools.title: type a command into a shell at its prompt
tools.description: Types `command` into the shell `terminal` at its prompt, through the shell, preserving history, and returns the id of the last completed block without waiting for the command. The shell needs OSC 133 shell integration. Read the command's output with `terminal_read` and its `last` mode once it is done. Called as a tool, run refuses while a command attn typed into that shell has not finished: read the terminal, and run again once it shows its prompt. On the CLI the command waits for it. Anyone may run a command in a shell.

desktop.description: the terminal's desktop, when it is not yours

terminal.description: A terminal id or a unique prefix of one, as terminal_ls lists them. A live session's name, its short id, full id or unique prefix of it, or a crew member's name, works when that session shows in exactly one terminal. Only terminals of your profile.

tools.name: terminal_send
tools.title: type text or keys into a terminal
tools.description: Types into `terminal` as a keyboard does: `text` as literal bytes, without Enter, or `keys` by name: C-a through C-z, C-\\, C-], C-^, C-_, Escape, Enter, Tab, Backspace, Space, Up, Down, Left, Right, Home, End, Delete, Insert, PageUp, PageDown, F1 through F12. Anyone may type into a shell; into an agent only when it is you or below you in your delegation chain, or you are the profile's chief.

desktop.description: the terminal's desktop, when it is not yours

keys.description: the keys to press, in order

terminal.description: A terminal id or a unique prefix of one, as terminal_ls lists them. A live session's name, its short id, full id or unique prefix of it, or a crew member's name, works when that session shows in exactly one terminal. Only terminals of your profile.

tools.name: terminal_read
tools.title: read a terminal's screen, scrollback or last command
tools.description: Returns the rendered screen of `terminal`; with `mode`, the retained scrollback, of which `lines` selects the last n lines, or the last completed command's block, which needs OSC 133 shell integration.

lines.description: the last lines of the scrollback

mode.description: read the last completed command's block, or the scrollback, instead of the screen

terminal.description: A terminal id or a unique prefix of one, as terminal_ls lists them. A live session's name, its short id, full id or unique prefix of it, or a crew member's name, works when that session shows in exactly one terminal. Only terminals of your profile.

tools.name: terminal_move
tools.title: move a terminal to another desktop
tools.description: Moves `terminal`, or your own session's terminal, to `desktop`: its shortcut digit, its name as shown or its id. A missing numbered desktop is created. The terminal keeps running beside the destination's active tile. Anyone may move a shell; an agent only when it is you or below you in your delegation chain, or you are the profile's chief.

terminal.description: the terminal to move; yours by default

tools.name: terminal_close
tools.title: close a shell
tools.description: Closes the shell `terminal`. It closes shells only; close an agent with `agent_close`.

desktop.description: the shell's desktop, when it is not yours; the refusal names the value to pass

terminal.description: A terminal id or a unique prefix of one, as terminal_ls lists them. A live session's name, its short id, full id or unique prefix of it, or a crew member's name, works when that session shows in exactly one terminal. Only terminals of your profile.

tools.name: turn_open
tools.title: ask for the user; the turn opens when you stop
tools.description: Asks for the user. When a notification from attn started your run, your stop may not put you in the user's queue, so open your turn before you stop to bring them something you need or finished. Run while you work, it opens your turn when you stop, so the user is not sent to you while you are still busy. A later notification does not settle a turn you opened; the user does, or `turn_settle`. For a decision only the user can make, use `ask` instead, whether or not you can keep working meanwhile.

tools.name: turn_settle
tools.title: settle a turn you opened, or cancel one that was going to open
tools.description: Settles a turn you opened, or cancels one that was going to open when you stop. A turn that opened when you stopped on your own is the user's to settle.

tools.name: vent
tools.title: record what got in your way; nobody replies
tools.description: Records a vent about attn's usability: an attn command that failed or behaved differently from its help or docs, attn instructions that contradict each other or attn's behavior, an attn capability you needed and had to work around, or attn not working inside your harness. With `about` tools, when the user turned tool vents on, it is about your other tooling instead: a skill, another CLI or MCP server, or your harness's permissions; the task and the repository are never tools. Don't vent because the work was hard, to report progress, or to ask for help. Say what happened, what you expected and what you did instead, in a paragraph at most. Nobody replies, so keep working. One vent per turn: to add to one, withdraw it with `vent_withdraw` and send one that covers both; withdraw a wrong vent instead of sending a correction.

about.description: What the vent is about: attn for attn itself, including attn blocked inside your harness, or tools for your other tooling (skills, other CLIs or MCP servers, harness permissions).

text.description: the vent, required; at most 16384 bytes

tools.name: vent_withdraw
tools.title: take back a vent you sent
tools.description: Takes back a vent this session sent.

vent.description: the vent's id, as recording it printed
